stories.title: GLM > GPT? GLM-5.2 passes vibe check; Z.ai forecasts Open Fable by December
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
GLM-5.2 from Zhipu AI is circulating with enough positive informal evaluations that Z.ai — the lab behind it — is now publicly forecasting a frontier-class open model called Open Fable by December 2025.

↳ THE REAL STORY
The 'vibe check' framing matters here: GLM-5.2 is not topping formal benchmarks in a way that dominates headlines, but practitioners running it on real tasks are reporting results competitive with GPT-class models. That gap between benchmark performance and actual usability is exactly where open models have historically lost ground. If GLM-5.2 is closing it, the practical implication is a credible open-weight alternative for teams who want to self-host a model that doesn't embarrass itself on production workloads. The Open Fable forecast adds a roadmap dimension — Z.ai is signaling they intend to stay on the frontier curve, not just ship a one-off competitive release.
stories.considerations: The catch is that 'vibe check' is doing a lot of work in this story. Informal consensus among practitioners is a real signal, but it is also the easiest thing to manufacture through selective sharing and cherry-picked demos. GLM-5.2 needs rigorous, reproducible evaluation across diverse tasks before the 'GLM > GPT' framing holds up. The December Open Fable forecast is also a hostage to fortune — Chinese labs have made ambitious timeline commitments before that quietly slipped. Worth watching whether independent evaluators publish structured comparisons in the next few weeks, and whether Z.ai releases model weights with enough openness to actually run at scale outside their own infrastructure.

stories.title: The Professor of Outputmaxxing — Anjney Midha, AMP
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
Latent Space published a long-form interview with Anjney Midha, partner at a16z's AMP (AI & ML Practice), covering his investment thesis and portfolio — which includes Anthropic, Mistral, Black Forest Labs, and Periodic Labs.

↳ THE REAL STORY
The excerpt is thin on technical substance — this is a founder/investor origin story episode, not a product announcement. The signal worth extracting: Midha's portfolio choices (Anthropic for frontier safety-adjacent bets, Mistral for open-weight European infrastructure, Black Forest Labs for image generation at the model layer) sketch a deliberate hedge across closed, open, and modality-specific AI stacks. For practitioners, the 'outputmaxxing' framing in the title hints the conversation touches on inference efficiency and throughput optimization — a topic with direct relevance to anyone running models at scale — though the raw excerpt doesn't confirm how deep that thread goes.
stories.considerations:
↳ WORTH WATCHING
The actual technical content of this episode is unverifiable from the excerpt alone — 'outputmaxxing' could mean anything from serious inference engineering discussion to a loose metaphor for productivity. Before treating this as a must-listen for developers, it's worth checking whether the episode delivers concrete frameworks or stays at the level of portfolio storytelling. Investor podcasts have a structural incentive to be interesting without being specific — the companies named are real bets, but the 'secret master plan' framing is a flag that the substance may be thinner than the guest list suggests.

stories.title: datasette-acl 0.6a0
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
datasette-acl 0.6a0 ships with expanded permission scope — moving beyond table-level access control toward a general resource-sharing system across Datasette instances.

↳ THE REAL STORY
Previously, datasette-acl let you lock down individual tables. This release broadens the model so permissions can apply to other resource types within Datasette — meaning teams running shared Datasette instances can start managing access to queries, databases, or other objects without hacking around the plugin's original table-only assumptions. For anyone building multi-user Datasette deployments, this is the groundwork that makes proper role-based access actually feasible rather than a workaround.
stories.considerations: The 'a0' alpha tag is doing real work here — this is pre-release infrastructure, not something to drop into production yet. The excerpt cuts off mid-sentence ('allow multi-user...'), which means the full scope of what's being built isn't public yet. Worth watching the GitHub releases closely: if Willison and Garcia are fleshing out a general sharing system, the design decisions made now will define what multi-tenancy looks like in Datasette for a long time.
